channel.title: Block Club Chicago - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Block Club Chicago (blockclubchicago.org)

item.title: Missing ‘Nerdette’? Greta Johnsen Is Back With ‘Happy To Be Here,’ A New And Still Nerdy Podcast
item.description: The podcast launches Friday and will feature conversations with authors, activists and journalists; monthly book club discussions; and recaps of the 1994 ABC drama "My So-Called Life."

item.title: Lawyers Race To Free Detained Immigrants – Before They’re Flown Away
item.description: During its immigration crackdown, the Trump administration has hurried to arrest, move and even deport thousands of people before they appear in court. But more than 100 in Illinois have won their release through a special petition.

item.title: How Chicago’s Bike Courier Collective Is Surviving The Age Of DoorDash And Delivery Robots
item.description: Cut Cats Couriers, one of Chicago’s last bike delivery companies, has provided personalized service across the city since 2012: "We're really good at it — like, stupid good at it."

item.title: Chicago’s ‘You Name A Snowplow’ Contest Returns. Here’s How To Submit And Vote
item.description: Submissions for the city's fourth annual snowplow naming contest are being accepted online through Jan. 10. The public will vote in February for the six winners.

item.title: Englewood Rapper And Farmer Heavy Crownz Taps Into His Roots For Debut Album
item.description: Ahead of the February release of “Trench Baby Turned Farmer,” Crownz created an immersive exhibit inspired by his love of farming, and will host a musical event there Friday.

item.title: Mayor’s Team Slams Alternative Budget, But Head Tax-Free Package Advances To Full City Council
item.description: The council-backed plan would lead to a $163 million shortfall and potential cuts next year, Mayor Brandon Johnson's administration said Wednesday. Alderpeople pressed on regardless, confident in their numbers.

item.title: CTA Closed Englewood’s Racine Green Line Station Over 30 Years Ago. By 2029, It Could Reopen
item.description: The 63rd and Racine Green Line station closed permanently in 1994 despite community pushback. A new transit bill signed by Gov. JB Pritzker requires that a renovated or newly built station open by January 2029.

item.title: Drawing Inspiration From Mentors, This Undocumented Artist Is Rekindling Her Passion
item.description: The 23-year-old never thought she could become an artist — but that changed when she met other Latino creatives.

item.title: Berwyn Woman Demands $1.5 Million After Being Shot By Agents At Broadview Protest
item.description: Ashley Vaughan says she suffered a concussion, chemical burns and contusions after being shot multiple times by federal agents. Since the incident she continues to suffer with chronic pain, migraines, vision sensitivity and mobility limitations.

item.title: Police Watchdogs Seek Hearing On Police’s Interactions With Feds After Bovino Thanks Officers
item.description: The call for the public hearing comes after Border Patrol chief Greg Bovino said on Wednesday that local police "cleared the way" for them to conduct immigration enforcement.
